In ancient Greece , a genos ( Greek : γένος, "race, stock, kin", [ 1 ] plural γένη genē ) was a social group claiming common descent, referred to by a single name (see also Sanskrit " Gana "). Most gene were composed of noble families—Herodotus uses the term to denote noble families—and much of early Greek politics seems to have involved struggles between gene . Gene are best attested in Athens , where writers from Herodotus to Aristotle dealt with them. [ citation needed ]
